statement: A member trained with difficulty-targeted reweighting (upweighting covariate-locatable hard rows) is more often correct on the champion's shared-fail pairs than the champion, and improves the portfolio when added.
mechanism: sample_weight = f(inner-cross-fitted difficulty score) for the member's FIT rows; a reweighted LGBM on the rich 285-feat view. New inductive bias (training-distribution reweighting), not a hyperparameter sweep.
evidence: Atlas: 85.3% of residual AUC mass is shared (route+aux fail the same pair); shared difficulty is covariate-predictable at AUC 0.9318 (set A, rich view only, SE 0.0002, satisfaction context only 0.534); teacher-confident-wrong 5.0x enriched on top-burden rows (novel structure, possibly irreducible).
admissibility: NOT closed. Reweighting is not in the closed list (generic GBDT sweeps, DART, RF, Ordered CatBoost, key TE, TabR, original appending, distillation, pseudo-labels, SSL32, TabPFN Fast, 2->4 estimators, 80->90% context, H18-C key-TE, H18-B stump, probability/rank averaging, imported stacks). Distinct from H18-B (stump = weaker member) and A1/A2 (residual-as-input-feature).
leakage_control: Difficulty score for each FIT row MUST come from an INNER cross-fit of the difficulty model within the FIT fold (mirrors TE inner cross-fitting). The Atlas outer pred_a is NOT usable as training weights (its training folds include the eval fold -> eval-fold label leak). Inner cross-fit keeps it fold-safe.
falsifying_experiment: Fold 0 only. (1) Inner-cross-fit difficulty model on FIT fold 0 (folds 1-4) -> per-row difficulty weights. (2) Train baseline LGBM (rich view, uniform weights) on folds 1-4 -> AUC on fold 0. (3) Train identical LGBM with hard-row upweighting -> AUC on fold 0. (4) On fold 0 shared-fail pairs (from Atlas), count specialist-correct vs champion-correct. Decision: if specialist is not better on fold-0 eval AND not right on shared-fail pairs -> DEAD. If it shows a path -> proceed to folds 1-4 + portfolio.
decision_rule: Admission (frozen): mean paired fold gain >= 1.5e-5 AUC, >= 2.5x paired SE, positive in >= 4/5 folds, vs current stack. Fold-0 falsification precedes any replication.

statement: The aux10 test-time deployment policy (single full-label fit) is worse than a bag-of-fold-models on a held-out pseudo-test, matching the S6E9 coverage lesson (+2.6e-4).
mechanism: OOF validates fold-fit members (80% FIT); test uses a single full-fit member (100%). Compare on a pseudo-test carved from train: (a) bag-of-5 fold-fit members vs (b) single full-fit member, both predicting the same pseudo-holdout.
evidence: Cross-season S6E9 lesson: deployment bagging-policy change moved both frozen finalists +2.6e-4 private. The aux10 test policy is asymmetric with OOF (100% vs 80%). The route side already matches (5 outer-FIT contexts at 80% both OOF and test); the aux10 side does not.
admissibility: NOT closed. Deployment-policy axis (19-E) is distinct from model/feature axes. S6E9 precedent is the strongest transferable policy signal.
leakage_control: No label leak: retraining on train subsets and predicting a held-out pseudo-test. Pseudo-test labels never enter training or selection.
falsifying_experiment: Carve a pseudo-test from train (e.g. fold 4 held out). Train the 5 fold-fit members on folds 0-3 (inner split) and the full-fit member on folds 0-3. Predict the pseudo-test with (a) the bag and (b) the full-fit. Compare AUC. Decision: if bag <= full-fit, the asymmetry is not a liability -> no change. If bag > full-fit, quantify the delta for finalist-selection consideration.
decision_rule: PSEUDO-TEST standard (not OOF-gate): this changes test predictions only, OOF is unchanged. Cannot pass the OOF admission gate. S6E9 warns pseudo-test deltas do not transfer to private; treat as a robustness signal for finalist selection, not an OOF promotion.

statement: A smoothed (nearest-key) rating-tuple generalization improves the unique-rating-key subpopulation (36% of rows, port AUC 0.95032) where exact-match TE is provably useless.
mechanism: For a row with rare rating key K, borrow label signal from rows with similar (not identical) keys. Fold-safe via inner cross-fitting.
evidence: Atlas segments: unique_rating_key subset AUC 0.95032 (254,260 rows = 36%), below overall 0.9619. Largest contiguous weak region. H18-C closed EXACT key-TE (+6.8e-6, insufficient); nearest-key is a different (smoothed) mechanism.
admissibility: PARTIALLY adjacent to closed H18-C (exact key-TE). Nearest-key smoothing is distinct but the prior is very low: members already see all 13 ratings and can generalize across similar keys via splits; a smoothed key adds little the member cannot derive.
leakage_control: Nearest-key label borrowing must use inner-cross-fitted labels within the FIT fold (mirrors TE). No eval-fold label enters.
falsifying_experiment: Fold 0 only. Add a nearest-key smoothed TE feature (inner-cross-fitted) to the rich view; train baseline vs +feature LGBM; measure AUC overall AND on the unique-key subset of fold 0. Decision: if no gain on the unique-key subset -> DEAD (the members already generalize).
decision_rule: Admission (frozen): mean paired fold gain >= 1.5e-5 AUC, >= 2.5x paired SE, positive in >= 4/5 folds. Given low prior, fold-0 falsification is the likely stopping point.

statement: A third diverse member breaks aggregation-loss ties (pairs where one half is right but the 50/50 average is wrong).
mechanism: Champion-B search: a member strong AND decorrelated enough on aggregation-loss pairs to shift the average toward the correct answer.
evidence: Atlas: aggregation_loss_auc_mass 0.0056 (15% of residual). Route-only 0.0059 + aux-only 0.0060 mass is the disagreement pool.
admissibility: NOT closed, but UNRESOLVED. All measured members are >=0.995 logit-correlated with champion and weaker. Phase 7 showed decorrelation (0.87) is insufficient if the member is weak. No candidate qualifies.
falsifying_experiment: None (no candidate). Champion B remains UNRESOLVED. Do not invent a hedge.
decision_rule: Frozen admission gate if a candidate ever emerges.

statement: A materially different neural architecture (TabM/RealMLP variant) reaches champion-level standalone AUC and enters the ensemble.
mechanism: Neural inductive bias on the rich view.
evidence: Neural prior strongly negative: RealMLP full view 0.960789-0.960881 (4 seeds), TabM 0.960693, corrected RealMLP f0 0.960758 -- all ~1e-3 below champion 0.961853. H18-B showed a weaker member (-1.88e-5) hurts the portfolio.
admissibility: NOT closed, but strongly negative prior. The audit disproven 'neural lacked the rich view' (historical members already used it). No evidence a variant reaches 0.9618+.
falsifying_experiment: None planned (negative prior does not justify GPU spend). Reopen only with a concrete architecture hypothesis that plausibly closes a 1e-3 gap.
decision_rule: Frozen admission gate. Neural is a reserve with a strong negative prior.
